title: Compact stride-aware kernel chaining and async-CUDA-event overlap for multi-GPU inference
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Chat and low-latency completion workloads show high tail latency when models consist of many small compute layers (short sequence lengths or small microbatches) due to per-kernel launch overhead and blocking synchronization between compute kernels and NCCL collectives. This PR introduces a compact, stride-aware kernel-chaining runtime path plus a lightweight async-CUDA-event overlap mechanism to reduce per-token latency and improve utilization for multi-GPU tensor-parallel inference. Approach: 1) Add a kernel-chaining ABI that allows consecutive small ops within the same inference step to be launched as a single chained launch path when they meet stride and memory-hint heuristics; the ABI exposes a 'chainable' hint at operator registration time and a compact launch planner that produces merged kernel groups. 2) Use non-blocking CUDA events and a per-device 'handoff' stream to decouple kernel launch ordering from NCCL collective dispatch, enabling overlap of local compute and inter-GPU communication without introducing busy-waiting. 3) KV cache prefetch adjustments: the cache prefetcher now recognizes chained regions and postpones aggressive eviction while chained launches are in-flight to reduce redundant reloads; it also inserts small prefetch windows between chained groups to keep memory pressure bounded. 4) Scheduler integration: the chain scheduler is a lightweight policy in the runtime scheduler that prefers chaining when anticipated savings (launch overhead + extra latency from cache thrash) exceed a tunable threshold. Back-compat and safety: Chain path is opt-in via per-model config (runtime.chain.enabled) and is guarded by runtime checks for deterministic ordering. Fallback to existing launch path retains identical semantics. Testing & results: microbench (small-batch chat with 8 token responses) shows 15-28% p95 reduction across our internal TPU-equivalent and multi-GPU setups for medium models (7B-30B) and a 7-12% tokens/sec cost reduction on typical continuous-batching traffic. Stress tests run for 72 hours without deterministic correctness regressions; KV cache metrics show 4-6% less eviction churn for chained workloads. This change also reduces overall kernel-launch counts by ~22% in observed traces. Implementation notes: new header runtime/kernel_chain.h, CUDA core in runtime/kernel_chain.cu, scheduler integration in runtime/scheduler/chain_scheduler.cpp, KV prefetcher updates in runtime/kv_cache/prefetcher.cpp, lightweight python bindings for toggling in bindings/python/chain_api.py, new perf harness tests, and docs. See release notes for config knobs and recommended thresholds.
commits_summary: Commit 1: add kernel_chain ABI and minimal planner; Commit 2: implement chained launch path and event-based overlap; Commit 3: integrate chain scheduler policy and heuristics; Commit 4: KV cache prefetcher awareness and metrics; Commit 5: perf tests, docs, and python bindings; Commit 6: followup fixes from reviewers (ordering, corner-case evictions); Commit 7: CI perf tuning and stability fixes.

ci_summary: CI: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass), gpu-integration (pass), perf-regression (pass after second run), lint (pass), flake8 (pass). One flaky microbench re-run required; green on re-run.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge. Commit message: 'runtime: compact stride-aware kernel chaining + async cuda event overlap (ENG-1289)'.
release_notes: - Introduces compact stride-aware kernel chaining to reduce kernel-launch overhead for workloads with many small ops. - Adds async CUDA event overlap to overlap local compute and NCCL collectives. - KV cache prefetcher is aware of chained regions to reduce eviction churn. - Config knobs: runtime.chain.enabled (bool), runtime.chain.min_stride (int), runtime.chain.memory_budget_mb (int), runtime.chain.overlap_threshold_ms (float). - Behavior is opt-in and falls back to the original launch path.
notes_for_ops: Recommend enabling on staging with runtime.chain.memory_budget_mb=128 and runtime.chain.min_stride=3; monitor chain_abort_reasons and chain_comm_overlap_ms; roll out via canary on 10% traffic before full rollout.
performance_summary: p95 latency reduction: 15-28% on small-batch chat; tokens/sec improvement: 7-12% on continuous batching; kernel-launches reduced by ~22%; KV eviction churn reduced by 4-6% for chained workloads.
